data.body:
Live Jira validation evidence (probe created, used, and removed from BOTH systems).

PROBE LIFECYCLE
- Probe rebar ticket a4d6-d6c4-e269-40e2 ("RBPROBE-4e21 soft-wrap validation probe (DELETE ME)") created with a deliberately hard-wrapped description.
- The reconcile bridge synced it to live Jira as REB-1585.
- Removed from rebar: `rebar delete a4d6-d6c4-e269-40e2 --user-approved` -> "Deleted ticket".
- Removed from Jira: `DELETE /rest/api/3/issue/REB-1585` -> HTTP 204; refetch returns "Issue does not exist".
- Verified clean: `rebar search "RBPROBE"` -> []; JQL `project=REB AND text ~ "RBPROBE"` -> 0 matches.
- Residue disclosed: the binding a4d6-d6c4-e269-40e2 -> REB-1585 remains in .bridge_state/bindings.json. BindingStore.unbind() was applied three times but the authoritative copy on the `tickets` branch is restored by the ~7-minute bridge pass faster than it can be committed. Both sides of the binding are deleted so it is inert (subsequent passes report "steady-state pass converged" with no error referencing it). Not force-fixed because hand-committing to the shared production `tickets` branch while the bridge is running is riskier than the residue.

END-TO-END BEHAVIOUR VALIDATED ON A REAL SYNCED ISSUE (REB-1159, local fd84-ba00-ba00-4f73)
Pass 1 (migration): `rebar reconcile --mode live --filter-local-ids fd84-ba00-ba00-4f73`
  -> "RECON: outbound_update key=REB-1159 changed=[description]"
  -> "RECON: batch_outcome action=update key=REB-1159 error=None"
  -> "OK: applied 1 of 1 mutations"
  Jira ADF before: 228 top-level nodes, Counter({'paragraph': 228}).
  Jira ADF after : 21 top-level nodes; soft-wrapped prose rejoined into single paragraphs; 215 hardBreak nodes retained inside list/code blocks so intentional line structure survives.

Pass 2 (convergence / no churn):
  -> no "changed=[description]" emitted for REB-1159.
  -> Jira description ADF sha256 identical across pass 1 and pass 2 (4ab0e8df2bd9587c, 21 nodes both times).

Echo check (no inbound clobber of the local store):
  local description sha256 BEFORE = 092ebb828a48b818 (275 lines)
  local description sha256 AFTER  = 092ebb828a48b818 (275 lines)
  -> byte-identical; the joined Jira body is NOT written back over the hard-wrapped local text.

ORIGINAL DEFECT CONFIRMED LIVE (pre-fix)
REB-1581 fetched read-only: 27 top-level nodes, all `paragraph`, one prose paragraph split across four nodes of 102/108/106/111 chars, with markdown `#`/`##` arriving as literal text.

DESIGN NOTE CAUGHT BY THIS LIVE RUN
The first implementation normalized the REMOTE value at the outbound compare sites too. Proven wrong on real data: REB-1581's body decodes to 27 lines raw vs 18 normalized, so normalizing both sides makes a stale old-format body compare EQUAL to local and no already-synced description would ever be repaired. Corrected to an asymmetry - outbound normalizes local only (so stale bodies are rewritten once, then converge); inbound normalizes both sides for the comparison only (so no echo). Unit tests were green either way; only the live check exposed it.

GATES
Gerrit change 982: LLM-Review +1, Verified +1, submitted, MERGED as 992b0656d on gerrit/main.
Unit suite 1433 passed; held-out RED->GREEN oracle tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/mutate/test_adf_soft_wrap.py 15/15, confirmed RED first and returned to RED under defect-seeded mutation.
